title: Sin's two aspects: foulness and obligation to penalty
source_text: V. Verum ut distinctius intelligatur quomodo Christus tollat hominum peccata, observandum est in peccato duo esse. Unum est pravitas & foeditas quaedam, quae peccatorem maculat & deturpat, Deoque odiosum reddit, ac rationi & legi divinae adversatur: Alterum est obligatio & ordinatio ad poenam quam justitia divina exigit, & lex interminatur.
pass_a_gloss: But that it may be understood more distinctly how Christ takes away men's sins, it is to be observed that there are two things in sin. One is a certain depravity and foulness, which stains and defiles the sinner, renders him hateful to God, and is contrary to reason and the divine law: The other is an obligation and ordination to the penalty which divine justice exacts and the law threatens.
pass_b_english: Sin has two sides: moral foulness that stains and God-hates, and obligation to the law's due penalty.
